content.comment_body: Hello everyone, hope you're well! I am using [product_name] and [product_name] [version_no]. I am testing both the webserver and the Android app. Is there a way to view the [product_name] display on a smartphone using the app? Has anyone managed this? Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you and regards.
Are you familiar with this manual? [url]

Yes, thank you [user_name]. I've read that manual. I still want to know if it's possible to see the module's display on my smartphone. For example, I’ve set up alarms that show messages on the module’s screen for specific inputs, and I’d like those notifications to appear on my smartphone when I check the app for alarms or errors. Hope this clarifies what I’m looking for. Thanks and regards.

If you're using the module's webserver on your smartphone, you just need the module's IP address in your phone’s browser. That works on your home network. For Internet access, you'd need Dynamic DNS or a VPN tunnel, and configure port forwarding in your router. I haven’t personally tried this myself.
Thanks [user_name]. I’m not using Dynamic DNS or VPN. I have the module’s IP address and I’m accessing the webserver, so I’ll try it that way. Thanks for your quick response. Regards.

As previously mentioned, you need access to the module’s IP address, so you’ll want your networking setup to be correct. Ensure your phone and the module are on the same subnet. In the configuration software, go to Tools > Transfer > Access Control—the default is off, but you’ll see other permissions. Web Access mirrors the module interface, allowing you to interact with it as if you were physically there. It’s the quickest method, and you can use any browser-enabled device. To display text screens, remember to enable the Web Server option for each text screen property. Remote access from a different network will require proper routing and port forwarding, similar to CCTV setups (such as using Dynamic DNS or No-IP). I do this for clients using 3G and a hosting service. The app offers more features but requires more setup and purchase for each control; it also looks more refined. Sorry this is not a step-by-step guide.

Hi everyone, does this mean you can’t view the display using the Android app? You need the IP address and must use a browser to access the module’s screen on your smartphone—so you don’t actually need the app for this task. Is that correct?
See my simplified network diagram for reference. Also, check YouTube for some demonstration videos: [url]. Best of luck!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring straightforward ways to view the [product_name] display and receive alarm messages on their smartphones. There is uncertainty regarding whether the Android app can replicate the physical display or if browser-based webserver access is necessary. Comments reveal confusion about the differences and limitations of the app versus browser access, particularly for monitoring and remote notifications.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to view the [product_name] display and get real-time alarm/error alerts directly on their smartphone through the Android app, with the experience resembling interaction with the actual device.
